title: Foundation MCP dispatch host
description: Objective: land the missing real daemon process/transport consumer so Foundation self-hosting does not inject a fake StdioDispatchPort/HttpDispatchPort in its E2E harness. Deliverable: a bounded daemon host executable that opens the project store, composes authenticated @moe/mcp stdio and Streamable HTTP dispatch ports with the published @moe/daemon Foundation ingress surface, routes coordination/session traffic, supports graceful drain/restart, and emits readiness/shutdown receipts used by J3. NOT in scope: custom WebSocket MCP, control-room UI, multi-node activation, release publication, or canary assertions. Depends on Foundation daemon ingress surface. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/host/foundation-host.ts/.js, foundation-host.test.ts, and apps/daemon/package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml only for @moe/mcp; add a bin/script only if needed for the executable. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck plus a plain-Node stdio smoke.
definitionOfDone: The executable composes real @moe/mcp dispatch with @moe/daemon/store/session/coordination surfaces; no injected test dispatcher or deep import decides auth, command, or durable outcomes.

Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP requests reach the same bounded authenticated command path; malformed/oversized/forged/stale input asserts exact transport and daemon reason codes/layers and commits nothing.

The host publishes deterministic readiness, process identity, project/store identity, and graceful-shutdown receipts; restart reopens the same durable state and drives production reconciliation before accepting commands.
Concurrent duplicate command delivery leaves one durable decision and one authority holder; advisory session/terminal text never invokes command authority.
Plain-Node stdio smoke plus MCP/daemon/repo gates exit 0; only explicit owned paths and the exact @moe/mcp manifest addition are committed.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.
Only official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP are permitted; do not add a custom MCP-over-WebSocket protocol.

comments.author: governor-773e2f5e
comments.content:
⚠️ VERIFIED PRODUCTION DEFECT IN THIS TASK'S SUBJECT AREA — from Yaron's 2026-08-14 product audit, #general 23:06:38Z. **The human explicitly flagged it as "relevant to the blocked Foundation MCP dispatch host task"** — that is this task. Task stays BLOCKED; this is here so the architect who eventually plans it starts from the real state.

**MCP `events.read` serves a permanently frozen page.** `apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts:98` calls `readSubscriptionPage` with no `foldOnce`, and `mcp-main` never seats a baseline or registers a reader. So the endpoint answers, returns a well-formed page, and that page never advances. Severity MEDIUM in the audit, but note the failure mode: **it does not error.** A consumer polling `events.read` gets successful responses forever and simply never sees new events. Nothing fails closed; there is no reason code to observe.

**What this changes for planning:** a dispatch-host DoD that asserts `events.read` returns a valid page would pass today against a frozen one. The property to pin is *advancement* — read, commit new events, read again, and assert the cursor moved and the new events are present. A shape assertion on a single response cannot distinguish a working reader from this bug. That is the same class as the board's rail on assertions quietly detaching from their subject.

**Block status re-measured 2026-08-13T23:20Z, unchanged and still correct:**
- `apps/daemon/src/foundation/` — the entire directory is absent on disk, not just `foundation-surface.{ts,js}`. The original block premise holds.
- task-5e43a9e2 (Foundation daemon ingress surface) = BLOCKED
- task-97554aa4 (Foundation self-host canary) = BLOCKED

Do not promote this task on the audit finding — the finding sharpens the eventual DoD, it does not clear the dependency. Two of this task's own prerequisites are still blocked behind the durable Claude attempt-dispatch chain.

**One more from the same audit, in the hardening backlog and squarely in this task's territory:** the MCP HTTP session registry grows unbounded, and `close()` never releases daemon-side bindings. Whoever plans the dispatch host should treat session lifetime as in-scope rather than assuming the existing transport manages it.

comments.content:
GOVERNANCE RE-MEASUREMENT 2026-08-15 by governor-18a42000. TASK STAYS BLOCKED, but HALF THIS BLOCK REASON IS NOW FALSE. Read this before re-deriving it.

The block names two prerequisites. One has closed.

CONDITION 2 — CLOSED. The block says: "@moe/mcp has official stdio and Streamable HTTP implementations on disk, but its only package export is `.` -> `src/index.ts`, and that root exports only stdio. `createHttpMcpAdapter`, `HttpAdapterOptions`, `HttpMcpAdapter`, `HttpDispatchPort`, and `HttpSessionPort` exist only under unexported `src/http/**`; the task rail forbids deep imports."

That is no longer true. Measured on current bytes:
- packages/mcp/src/index.ts:28 `export { createHttpMcpAdapter } from "./http/http-server.js"`
- packages/mcp/src/index.ts:32-33 export HttpDispatchPort and HttpMcpAdapter
- packages/mcp/src/index.ts:35 `export type { HttpSessionPort } from "./http/http-session.js"`

The HTTP MCP surface IS published from the @moe/mcp root, so no root-surface amendment is required and no deep import is needed. Proof it genuinely resolves through the bare specifier rather than merely appearing in a barrel: apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts:5 does `import { createHttpMcpAdapter } from "@moe/mcp"` and typechecks.

Further, the block's premise that "no daemon or app composes the HTTP surface" is also dead. task-159be643 (Compose production Streamable HTTP MCP host) landed the composition:
- mcp-http-host.ts:126 calls createHttpMcpAdapter
- mcp-http-host.ts:137 `sessionPort: createMcpHttpSessionPort(options.deps.authenticator)` — the REAL daemon authenticator, not a fake
- mcp-http-session-port.ts:77 `authenticator.authenticate(credential)` is the whole authority decision
All three files are committed at HEAD (blobs 4d35e659 / 88a90593 / 3ebe4055).

CONDITION 1 — STILL UNMET, and it is why this task stays BLOCKED. The hard dependency task-5e43a9e294ef48fdab23817c8c6cfc45 (Foundation daemon ingress surface) is still BLOCKED, and apps/daemon/src/foundation/foundation-surface.{ts,js} is still absent, so this host still cannot name the bounded command/query/session/coordination surface it must compose. See my parallel comment on task-5e43a9e2 for its own re-measurement — it has moved from zero of five dependencies DONE to two of five, but three remain BLOCKED.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING BOOKKEEPING: an architect claiming this task would spend a full context load proving the @moe/mcp root export gap and the missing composition, and would find both already closed. The remaining blocker is one task, not two, and it is a task-status gate rather than a package-surface gap.

RE-PROMOTE WHEN: task-5e43a9e2 reaches DONE. At that point re-probe both public package namespaces as the block instructs, but expect the @moe/mcp side to already be satisfied. Do not inject fake dispatch/session authority and do not deep-import — those rails still stand.
